clue.text: Description of Grant's soldiers by mine host

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's soldiers who build and sap
mine host is the jocular old term for a pub landlord, a publican

explanation.surface: Someone describes the troops of a general, as seen by an innkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses S. Grant, the Union general, later became a US president from the Republican party. 'Grant's soldiers' wants to be read together; the split comes after 'Grant's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grant stood for president for the Republicans, so that party label describes him.

clue.text: Royal order for dress

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for royal, as in RN
the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A royal decree about what to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment, a kind of formal dress.

clue.text: It indicates a canine breed

explanation.surface: A pedigree dog shows which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle or stick that shows a reading is one sense; the other is a gun dog that freezes to show where game lies.

clue.text: Crooner's entry interrupted by hostile invective

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into it, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: the crooner is Bing Crosby, so his possessive gives Bing's
ill as in ill will means hostile
a gate is a way in, an entry

explanation.surface: A singer's arrival on stage is spoilt by hostile shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate, the old London fish market, gave its name to coarse abusive language. 'interrupted by' splits the crooner's name after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The fishwives of the London market were famed for foul language, so their market's name came to mean vulgar abuse.

clue.text: Inserts supplied by one writing about industrial equipment

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the writing goes round the equipment

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
plant is the machinery used in industry

explanation.surface: Inserts are provided by a person writing about factory machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Implants are things put into the body surgically, so they are inserts.

clue.text: Beginning of play about a military engagement

parts.note: the opening section of a stage play is Act I
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: The opening scene of a drama concerns a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a fight between armed forces, a battle or engagement.

clue.text: Many involved in rescue, mostly East European

indicators.note: one thing involved in another is caught up inside it
mostly means most of the word but not all, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to save is to rescue
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, crosswords' standard 'many'

explanation.surface: A crowd joins a rescue, mostly people from Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SAVE to SAV; 'involved in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavs are the peoples of eastern Europe speaking Slavonic languages, such as Poles and Russians.

clue.text: Publicity on one of the branches?

explanation.surface: An advertisement pinned to a tree branch.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical second reading: a tiny leaf, as found on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed handbill is promotional material; the second sense is a small leaf or one segment of a compound leaf.

clue.text: Loved piece, maybe? It transported our forebears

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be put another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cherished item, possibly the vehicle that carried our ancestors.
explanation.walkthrough: A velocipede is an early bicycle, such as the boneshaker or penny-farthing.
explanation.definitionFit: Early pedal cycles of the nineteenth century carried people of past generations around.

clue.text: Where an unemployed Irishman in Bangor rode horses originally?

definitions.text: Where an unemployed Irishman in Bangor rode horses originally?

indicators.note: in places the idle Irishman inside the string of opening letters
originally points to the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: idle means out of work, unemployed
Pat, short for Patrick, is the crossword's stock Irishman

explanation.surface: A jobless Irishman in a Welsh town once rode horses somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'Bangor rode horses' give BRH; 'in' puts IDLEPAT between BR and H. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A track meant for riders on horseback is exactly where a man might go riding.

clue.text: Wrestling-throw? An easy victim, this guy

explanation.surface: A wrestler throws a gullible opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this guy' completes the phrase fall guy, a dupe or scapegoat.
explanation.definitionFit: In wrestling a pin of the opponent's shoulders counts as a fall; a fall guy is an easy dupe.

clue.text: Customary, note to politician providing illumination

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a thing that gives light

parts.note: standard means usual, customary
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: The usual message to an MP shedding light on things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the object does rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall floor-standing lamp gives light to a room.

clue.text: It's the case when odd characters abandon beat music

indicators.note: the odd-numbered characters leave, so only the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters stay

explanation.surface: It is the situation when strange types quit pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' sounds like eccentric people, but means the letters in odd positions.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: So topical, somehow, yet contemporary with the disciples

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A current affairs topic, oddly enough, dates from the time of the disciples.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostolic means of the apostles, so belonging to their era.

clue.text: At least one delivery is made here

definitions.text: At least one delivery is made here

parts.words: At least one delivery is made here
parts.note: delivery suggests post or goods, but it is the delivery of a baby, which happens once at the place in question

explanation.definitionFit: The place where someone is born is where at least one birth, a delivery, occurred.

clue.text: Angry about trick to supply with water

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the angry word goes round the trick

parts.note: irate means angry
to rig is to fix dishonestly, a trick

explanation.surface: An angry man rigs things in order to water his land.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrigating land means channelling water onto it.

clue.text: Member partly conforming with others

explanation.surface: A club member falls partly into line with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' here is a limb: the arched part of the foot is only part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched middle of the foot is part of a limb; marching in step means keeping in line with the others.

clue.text: Broad view of girl kept by parents

indicators.note: something kept by others is held inside them

parts.note: pa and ma, father and mother, are the parents
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wide outlook on a daughter living with her mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide unbroken view of a landscape.

clue.text: He's escaped' from the bully-boy's feeding-place

indicators.note: something that has escaped from a place is no longer in it, so those letters go

parts.note: a rough is a thug, a bully-boy, so the bully-boy is the rough
he has, read as the letters of the pronoun

explanation.surface: A man has got away from a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation mark after 'escaped' is a printing quirk.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long container holding food or water for animals.

clue.text: Continental city newly associated with Jelly Roll Morton?

definitions.text: Continental city newly associated with Jelly Roll Morton?

parts.words: Continental city newly associated with Jelly Roll Morton?
parts.note: a French city which, with 'new' put before it, becomes the American birthplace of the jazz pianist Jelly Roll Morton

explanation.definitionFit: The French cathedral city on the Loire, prefixed by new, names Morton's Louisiana home town.

clue.text: Steps taken, by a Bedouin perhaps, in the desert?

indicators.note: in means the Bedouin is placed inside the desert

parts.note: the desert is sand
a Bedouin is one kind of Arab, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Dance moves performed by a nomad out in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A saraband is a stately Spanish dance, a sequence of dance steps.

clue.text: Opposite to Latin elegiacs, for example

parts.note: ad is the Latin word for to
elegiacs are a classical metre, an example of verse

explanation.surface: Something is contrary to Latin poetry written in elegiacs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposite to' wants to be read together; the definition is just 'Opposite', and 'to' goes into Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means facing against, contrary, as with an adverse wind.

clue.text: Knave, say, on King is an excess of ambition

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: knave said out loud is nave, the hub of a wheel
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A jack, perhaps, laid on a king, is overreaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knave' suggests a playing card, but it is spoken as nave, the central part of a wheel, which is the hub.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is overweening pride, the arrogant ambition the Greeks said the gods punish.

clue.text: Controlling, committee built poor resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort the letters again

explanation.surface: A ruling committee put up a shabby holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but splits as re-sort; the comma after 'Controlling' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the supreme policy-making body of a Communist party.

clue.text: Peaceful flier lost height rapidly in the USA

definitions.text: lost height rapidly in the USA

explanation.surface: A bird of peace plunged down in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The white bird is a symbol of peace; Americans use it as the past tense of dive.

clue.text: Marbles set up to strike thus

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: taws are marbles, especially the shooter in the game

explanation.surface: Glass balls are arranged to be hit like this.
explanation.definitionFit: To swat is to hit sharply, as at a fly.

clue.text: A crazy set-back for a furniture designer

indicators.note: set back means the pieces are turned to run backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A mad setback hits a cabinet maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Adam was the 18th-century Scottish architect and designer whose style covered furniture. 'set-back' turns AMAD round.
explanation.definitionFit: The neoclassical designer Robert Adam created furniture and interiors.

clue.text: Street in Cumbrian town identifying British Government stores

indicators.note: in puts the street inside the town

parts.note: Barrow-in-Furness is a port in Cumbria, a county in north-west England
a road is a street

explanation.surface: A road in a north of England town marks official supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: The broad arrow is the arrowhead mark stamped on British government property, once on convicts' uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrowhead symbol was stamped on official property to show it belonged to the Crown.

clue.text: Direction to decapitate the brute

indicators.note: decapitating means cutting off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a beast is a brute

explanation.surface: An order to behead the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: East is a compass point, one of the cardinal directions.

clue.text: Geographical, feature recent : maps misrepresented

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown wrongly, so the letters are presented in another order

explanation.surface: A landscape feature is new, but the maps show it wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Geographical' and the colon are printing slips.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarpment is a long steep slope or cliff, a landform.
